topics.definition: Connecting residents to government and strengthening democratic participation.
Strengthening the structural foundations of democratic governance and institutions.
Transparency, open data, FOIA, and public accountability infrastructure.
Improving how government operates internally: processes, systems, and workforce efficiency.
Modernizing how government buys, evaluates vendors, and manages technology and service contracts.
Improving the speed at which government can respond to problems and opportunities.
Reducing unnecessary complexity in government rules, forms, procedures, and compliance requirements.
Improving resident access to and delivery of government benefit programs.
Human-centered design of government services, forms, processes, and digital interfaces.
Placing or mobilizing subject matter experts to work on government problems.
Redesigning how government structures its talent acquisition and retention systems.
Improving the mechanics of government recruitment, assessment, and onboarding.
Building pathways for technologists, policy experts, and public servants to enter government.
Upskilling existing government workers and the broader labor force served by government programs.
Breaking down fragmented data systems that prevent agencies from sharing information.
Protecting government systems and data from cyber threats.
Replacing or modernizing outdated government technology infrastructure.
Building reusable, open-source, or collectively-owned technology infrastructure for government.
Embedding research and data into government decision-making and program design.
Building mechanisms for government to collect and act on resident and stakeholder input.
Building government capacity to test, learn, and improve through iteration.
Using data and evidence to track and improve government program results.
Identifying proven approaches and systematically replicating them across jurisdictions.
Government adoption, governance, and responsible deployment of artificial intelligence.
Expanding government capacity to deploy and manage broadband infrastructure.
Technology and reform capacity for child protective services, foster care, and family systems.
Technology and reform capacity for law enforcement, courts, corrections, and reentry.
Government capacity for emergency management, disaster response, and 911 systems.
Government programs and systems that improve economic opportunity for residents.
Technology capacity for government education agencies to deliver and improve learning.
Technology capacity for government health programs: Medicaid, Medicare, public health delivery.

Modernizing government permitting, licensing, and code enforcement processes.
